name: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type II
aliases: HEMPAS (Hereditary Erythroblastic Multinuclearity with Positive Acidified Serum test)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type II

criteria.description: Presence of binucleated and multinucleated erythroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Hypoglycosylation of erythrocyte membrane proteins demonstrated by lectin binding assays or SDS-PAGE
Positive acidified serum test (HEMPAS test) indicating increased erythrocyte membrane fragility
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the SEC23B gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic bone marrow morphology plus either hypoglycosylation of erythrocyte membrane proteins or pathogenic SEC23B mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory but not always available; bone marrow findings are essential.

searchTerms: red blood cell precursors with two nuclei
defective sugar chains on red blood cells
low glycosylation on red cell surfaces

common.notes: Elevated reticulocyte count reflecting marrow response

occasional.notes: Due to ineffective erythropoiesis and transfusions

rare.notes: Rare but possible in severe cases
searchTerms: cardiac issues due to low red cells

rare.notes: Due to chronic anemia and marrow expansion

laboratory: Anemia with normocytic or macrocytic indices
imaging: Ultrasound showing splenomegaly and possible gallstones
other: Bone marrow aspirate showing binucleated and multinucleated erythroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: No hypoglycosylation of erythrocyte membrane proteins
Distinct bone marrow morphology with internuclear chromatin bridges
More severe anemia and ineffective erythropoiesis

redFlags: Severe anemia refractory to standard treatment
Signs of iron overload despite no transfusions
references: Iolascon A, et al. Congenital dyserythropoietic anemias: molecular insights and diagnostic challenges. Haematologica. 2020.
Heimpel H, et al. Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II: clinical and molecular aspects. Blood. 2018.
